=========================================================
WHO'S WHO IN CANADA (Toronto: International Press) — the entry for OWEN ERNEST OWENS
Internet Archive: whoswhoincanada0000unse_r1d7, scan leaf 1546, printed page 790.

NOT LENDING-RESTRICTED. The complete djvu text (5,050,896 bytes) was downloaded and searched.
"Kanawana" occurs exactly ONCE in the volume, in this entry.

ON THE VOLUME'S DATE. The Internet Archive gives 1911, which is the series' start and not this
volume. The entry's own latest datum is "Vice-President, Exploration, February 1976", so the volume
is 1976 or later — NOT the "Who's Who in Canada 1965" this project's p_429 called it. That earlier
description came from a search snippet in which the running head "IN CANADA" and the entry's own
"1965" fell side by side; the walk below shows they belong to different lines. **The 1965 in the
snippet is the year of his Kanawana directorship, not the volume's year.**

THIS RESOLVES p_429, which asked for the name of the unnamed Kanawana director on this leaf.


THE ENTRY, as printed (running heads "790 / WHO'S WHO" and "IN CANADA" have been lifted out of the
OCR stream where they interrupt the text; nothing else is altered):

    OWENS, Owen Ernest, Ph.D. — Vice-President, Exploration, Cominco Ltd. (est. 1906), mining and
    refining base metals, manufacturing chemicals and chemical fertilizers, 200 Granville Square,
    Vancouver, British Columbia V6C 2R2. Director: Vestgron Mines Limited (President); Arvik Mines
    Ltd. BORN MONTREAL, QUEBEC, MARCH 30, 1925. Educated: ST. GEORGES, MONTREAL, 1930-38;
    WESTMOUNT HIGH SCHOOL, 1938-43; McGILL UNIVERSITY, MONTREAL, B.Sc., 1948; M.Sc., 1951; Ph.D.,
    1955. Worked as geologist for Inspiration Mining & Development Co. Ltd., 1953-57; Joined Cominco
    in 1957 as geologist in mining division at Kimberley; Geologist, Exploration Division, Cominco,
    at Bathurst, New Brunswick, 1960; Exploration Division, Cominco, Montreal, 1960; Exploration
    Superintendent, Cominco, Eastern Division, 1963; Exploration Superintendent, Cominco,
    International, 1965; Manager, International Exploration, Cominco 1969; Assistant Director,
    Exploration, Cominco, 1970-71; Vice-President and Managing Director, Vestgron Mines Limited,
    1971-74; President, Vestgron Mines Limited, April 1974- ; Managing Director, Cominco Europe,
    June 1974-75; Director, Exploration, Cominco Ltd., July 1975; Vice-President, Exploration,
    February 1976. Member: C.I.M.M.; Geological Association of Canada. Clubs: Kimberley Ski
    (President, 1960); Redbirds Ski; **KAMP KANAWANA (YMCA), DIRECTOR, 1965.** Recreation: skiing.
    Married: ALISON MARY RAMSAY, 1952; has one son (DAVID NORREY) and two daughters (Jane Meredith
    and Nancy Margaret). Residence: 4638 Angus Drive, Vancouver, British Columbia V6J 4J5.


WHAT IT GIVES
-------------
A DIRECTOR OF KAMP KANAWANA IN 1965, NAMED, WITH A FULL BIOGRAPHY. He is a Montreal-born mining
geologist: St. George's School and Westmount High School, three McGill degrees ending in a 1955
doctorate, then a career with Cominco that runs from a Kimberley mining geologist in 1957 to
Vice-President for Exploration in 1976.

NOTE WHAT "DIRECTOR" MEANS HERE. It appears under **Clubs**, in a list with two ski clubs, and the
camp's own directors index has A. Ross Seaman as Camp Director from 1959 to 1967. So this is a
GOVERNANCE role — a director on the camp's committee or board — and not the summer directorship.
The entry also places him in Cominco's Montreal exploration office from 1960 and moving to the
international division in 1965, which fits a Montreal committee seat ending about then.


AND THE PART THAT BEARS ON THE ORDER OF OWENS
---------------------------------------------
`order-of-owens.md` establishes that the award's donor and presenter, "Norrey Owens", is
**O. N. H. Owens**, Chairman of the Kanawana Committee in the late 1930s and of Camp Perrot's board
through the 1940s and 50s. Its Open Question 1 asks for his full given names, and records an
unproven lead: that he is the "OWENS, OWEN NORREYS HARRINGTON" of a Library and Archives Canada
First World War file.

**Owen Ernest Owens's only son is named DAVID NORREY.**

Norrey is not a common given name. Its appearance as a middle name in a Montreal Owens family, one
generation below a man who was a Kanawana director in 1965 and two below a Kanawana Committee
chairman called Norrey, is real corroboration for reading O. N. H. as **Owen NORREYS Harrington**.

**IT IS NOT PROOF, AND NOTHING HERE SAYS THE TWO MEN ARE RELATED.** This project has no document
connecting Owen Ernest Owens (b. 1925) to O. N. H. Owens. What it has is a surname, a city, a camp,
and an uncommon family name recurring across the generations — which is a hypothesis worth stating
and testing, not a fact. The test is cheap for anyone with genealogical access: a Montreal birth
record for Owen Ernest Owens, 30 March 1925, would name his father.

The shape of the succession is also suggestive and equally unproven: O. N. H. Owens chairs the
Kanawana Committee from 1929 into the 1960s, and Owen Ernest Owens is a director of the camp in
1965.
